evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database analyzes 打 as formed from 手 with 丁 as phonetic, with basic sense ‘strike, knock, collide.’ It lists no oracle-bone or bronze examples and one small-seal entry. It cites a Han-period 王延壽 poem using 打 for striking, followed by examples for attack/fighting, making, and a prepositional use in other periods. These separate citations do not prove a direct chronological semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「打」

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The page reports two Guangyun entries, 德冷切 and 都挺切, categorized in Middle Chinese as 上聲 readings in the 庚/梗 division II and 青/迥 division IV respectively. It records these as distinct dictionary readings without establishing their semantic or dialectal distribution.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「打」

evidence.source: 徐時儀, 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微
evidence.text: The article states that 打 is absent from the received Shuowen and appears in the Song-era 徐鉉 New Attached section. It discusses early references attributed to 玄應 and 慧琳, including a 通俗文 gloss “撞出曰打,” but notes that witnesses and alleged Shuowen quotations do not securely establish the wording of an earlier Shuowen edition. The article therefore complicates any simple claim that the Song New Attached entry is the earliest extant lexical use.
evidence.title: 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微

evidence.source: 徐時儀, 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微
evidence.field: graphic history and proposed 木-form relation
evidence.text: The article reviews proposals linking 打 with forms written using 木 and later 手, including possible confusion or replacement. It concludes that the proposed identity is not established by surviving pre-Song dictionaries and rhyme books because recorded form, sound, or meaning differ. No particular corruption path or ancestor-descendant relationship is demonstrated.
evidence.title: 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry says 打 is not in the main Shuowen text but is in its New Attached section, analyzed 从手、丁聲 and glossed ‘strike’; it records 都挺切 as the older reading. This supports 手/扌 as the semantic component and 丁 as phonetic, but it does not establish an earlier graphic ancestor or corruption.
evidence.title: [A01498] 打 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry gives a Tang 杜甫 example for ‘strike,’ a Song 汪元量 example for ‘take/catch fish,’ and later examples for attack, making, buying, printing, and ‘from/since.’ These are dictionary examples rather than proof of the order or direct derivation of each sense. It separately treats Mandarin dǎ for the striking-related senses and dá as an English-dozen transliteration for twelve items.
evidence.title: [A01498] 打 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons, Ancient Chinese characters project
evidence.field: glyph image provenance and rights framework
evidence.text: The project describes its images as reusable educational graphics and states that project graphics are public domain, with attribution requested as a moral condition. It distinguishes script categories including Shuowen seal script and ancient artifact script traditions. This project information is general; the individual 打 file page supplies its own provenance and rights details.
evidence.title: Commons:Ancient Chinese characters project

evidence.field: glyph candidate, dating scope, provenance and rights
evidence.text: The file page describes a vector depiction of 打 in Shuowen seal-script style and cites Sinica Database, Chinese Etymology, the CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database, Chinese Text Project, and Chinese Linguipedia as available sources; it identifies the referenced hanziyuan image as S09107. The file is a modern Inkscape drawing, not a photograph or direct scan of an ancient artifact. The page states that the SVG representation is public domain; attribution is appreciated.

search_audit.outcome: Search performed; opened CUHK database, scholarly PDF, Taiwan MOE dictionary, and Sinica character record. CUHK page provides the 手 + 丁 phonetic analysis, one small-seal entry, no bronze/oracle examples in its displayed table, historical readings and dated lexical examples. The PDF discusses disputed early textual witnesses.

search_audit.outcome: Search found and opened the 打-seal.svg Commons description page. It identifies a Shuowen seal-style vector drawing, lists source databases, supplies a direct SVG link, and states public-domain status. No separate verified oracle or bronze artifact image candidate was established in this search.

gaps: The queried institutional form record shows a small-seal entry but no oracle-bone or bronze entry; this listing does not prove the graph was absent from all earlier writing.

Han-period literary use and early dictionary citations are mediated by later textual transmission. The opened scholarship flags uncertainty about alleged earlier Shuowen wording; manuscript-level verification remains unresolved.

The file candidate is a modern redraw labelled Shuowen seal style, not an ancient artifact photograph. Its associated exact artifact or manuscript exemplar and date are not established by the Commons file description.
The reviewed evidence does not support a graphic ancestor based on 木 or a specific corruption event; the proposed relationship remains disputed.
Separate period examples exist for striking, attacking/fighting, making, catching fish, and a prepositional use, but a complete chronological semantic chain has not been established.
The dozen-counter reading is explicitly distinguished as an English-dozen transliteration, but the opened references do not establish its first Chinese attestation or a dated intermediate form 打臣.

丁’s phonetic role is independently supported by the New Attached component analysis and the phonological evidence summarized in the dossier; historical reconstructions remain system-dependent and do not provide direct recordings of ancient pronunciation.

No proposed Mizo or Mon-Khmer comparison was independently checked against a primary comparative source in this invocation; source-word chronology, sound correspondences, borrowing direction, and cognacy remain unresolved.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; the drawing itself was uploaded in 2015 and is a modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of the Shuowen seal-script form of 打, showing the hand element alongside 丁, which the dictionary tradition analyzes as phonetic.
items.alt: Black seal-style strokes representing 打 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The only directly verified character-specific historical glyph candidate found. It illustrates the form described by the Shuowen New Attached entry and supports discussion of the hand and 丁 components, while its page explicitly labels it a modern vector depiction.
items.rights: Public domain according to the Commons file page; attribution appreciated.

limitations.text: This is a modern vector redraw in a historical script style, not a photograph or scan of an ancient artifact. The reviewed sources do not establish a dated sequence of earlier 打 forms; no oracle-bone or bronze candidate was verified.
